verdict.line: You lose when you feed him three stacks of An Acquired Taste and let him Devour you off a bad all-in; you win when you land E (Test of Spirit) and convert the spirit-rip into a tentacle burst before he can reset.

brief.thesis: This is close and data-even: Illaoi holds the lane and solo-kill edge (51.2% over 127 games), but the whole fight hinges on whether Tahm Kench reaches 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste before you land a clean E. His passive scales his damage off total health, so the longer the trade drags on, the more his raw stats start winning it for him — Illaoi needs to front-load damage through E and tentacles, not grind it out.

tell.watch: His An Acquired Taste stack count

theirWindow.when: he hits 3 stacks of his passive
theirWindow.what: At 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste he can Devour (R) you outright. Do not commit to a full all-in past this point unless you can kill through the Devour window — back off and reset instead of feeding him a free swallow.

yourWindow.when: your E (Test of Spirit) just landed
yourWindow.what: The ripped spirit echoes a percentage of damage back to the real target, and your tentacles swing at both the spirit and the victim. Immediately follow with Q (Tentacle Smash) and W (Harsh Lesson) while the spirit is still out — this is your highest-damage window in the entire trade.

start.why: The lifesteal and damage proc let you win extended auto-trades before E is online at level 3, which matters since his Q (Tongue Lash) outranges your early kit.

boots.why: His full kit (Q, W, R) deals magic damage, and the tenacity shortens how long his Q slow pins you for a follow-up stack.

core.why: Armor shred directly counters a passive that scales off his total health — the tankier he builds, the more this matters.
The slow-on-proc keeps him inside E (Test of Spirit) range and inside tentacle swing range during your burst window.
Highest measured win rate on this exact path (75% over 12 games) — the extra healing from tentacle procs and passive sustain offsets his poke.

situational.when: you're ahead and want to amplify the all-in once your tentacle burst lands
he out-trades you with Q poke before your E-spirit combo comes online
you're snowballing early kills and want to close the game out faster

runes.keystoneWhy: This is an extended-trade matchup built around landing and following up on E — Conqueror's stacking adaptive force and healing keep you ahead in the prolonged spirit-rip fight rather than a single burst window.

summoners.why: Teleport is the most-picked spell here (55.6% pick rate) because Illaoi's split-push and vessel pressure reward being able to return to a side lane after pushing it. If you want to deny his kill setup directly, Exhaust+Flash posted the highest measured win rate (62.5%) by neutralizing a Devour all-in.

playing.title: Poke with E, not autos, pre-6
playing.detail: E (Test of Spirit, range 900) matches his Q (Tongue Lash, range 900) in reach, so use it to start every trade rather than walking into auto range where he out-trades you.

playing.title: Combo off every landed E
playing.detail: The moment the spirit is ripped, follow with Q (Tentacle Smash) and W (Harsh Lesson) — tentacles swing at the spirit and the victim both, so this is where your damage actually comes from.

playing.title: Never all-in past 3 stacks
playing.detail: Track his An Acquired Taste count on his portrait. At 3 stacks he can Devour you for free; disengage or make sure you can kill through the swallow before committing further.

playing.title: Respect point-blank Q
playing.detail: His Q slows, heals him on champion hit, and stacks his passive. Don't stand still in his 900-range Q line while he's farming stacks for a Devour setup.

playing.title: Punish Abyssal Dive cooldown
playing.detail: W is on a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown with no other escape in his kit. Once you see him use it, that's your window to press a trade or roam without fear of a dive-away or dive-engage.

playing.title: Build through his HP, not around it
playing.detail: His passive damage scales off total health, so Black Cleaver's armor shred specifically undercuts the stat he's stacking for — prioritize it over flat damage items.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/sample numbers above are measured from live OP.GG data on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning (E-spirit burst windows, stack-count tracking, Cleaver countering his HP scaling) is this brief's own tactical read.

stats.opponentTip: Even after [E] land successfully, Tahm Kench can have the upper hand if he swallows with (W) when there are 4 stacks (P) to prevent being damaged further. Tahm Kench often gets his kills when he has a chance to swallow his enemies. Try not to be hit with (Q) in close range. Engage and aim for a kill only after purchasing items adequately to tank Tahm Kench’s damage.
